headline: Visayas Grid Under Red Alert; Mindanao on Yellow Alert
seoTitle: Visayas Grid Under Red Alert; Mindanao on Yellow Alert
seoDescription: NGCP extended the Visayas red alert through 9 p.m. and placed Mindanao under a yellow alert through 8 p.m. on August 12 as outages and deratings tightened supply.
deck: NGCP extended the Visayas red alert through 9 p.m. and placed Mindanao under a yellow alert through 8 p.m. as plant outages and deratings tightened electricity supply.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines placed the Visayas grid under a red alert and the Mindanao grid under a yellow alert on Wednesday, August 12, as unavailable generating capacity and high demand reduced power margins.
An afternoon update extended the Visayas red alert from 3 p.m. to 9 p.m., with yellow alerts from 1 p.m. to 3 p.m. and 9 p.m. to 10 p.m. Mindanao was under a yellow alert from 1 p.m. to 8 p.m.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Visayas grid had 2,153 megawatts of available capacity against projected peak demand of 2,394 MW. NGCP listed forced outages and derated plants totaling 931.5 MW of unavailable capacity.

Mindanao had 2,779 MW of available capacity against projected peak demand of 2,689 MW, with 621.6 MW unavailable. A red alert means supply is insufficient to meet demand and regulating requirements; a yellow alert means supply can meet demand but lacks the required contingency margin.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Consumers in the Visayas faced a heightened risk of rotational interruptions during the red-alert period, while Mindanao's reduced reserve margin left the grid more vulnerable to another plant failure or demand increase. An alert signals system conditions; actual interruption schedules remain the responsibility of distribution utilities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Monitor NGCP and local distribution-utility advisories for changes to alert hours and any interruption schedules. Restoration of unavailable units and lower-than-forecast demand could improve margins, while additional outages could extend the alerts.
